recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. If future work is needed for code-vs-identifier modeling on PackagedProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, or AdministrableProductDefinition, handle it under those resources' specific Jira decisions rather than this seed.
issue_request: FHIR-31794 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification BRR change request asking why medicinal product artifacts used identifiers rather than codes for NDC, RxNorm, and similar product-type concepts. The resolution requested a 0..* code attribute with an example binding alongside identifier and clearer definitions explaining when to use identifier, code, or both.
initial_application: The change was explicitly applied in git before this reconciliation: e640618988 added MedicinalProductDefinition.code as Coding 0..* with an example medication-codes binding, and cc9be95595/71a4873af9 clarified the MedicinalProductDefinition.identifier and .code definitions.
additional_context: The current build actively includes MedicinalProductDefinition, PackagedProductDefinition, ManufacturedItemDefinition, and AdministrableProductDefinition, while fhir.ini maps the old R4 MedicinalProduct* resource names to those R5/R6 successors. Later related work handled neighboring concerns separately: FHIR-31795 clarified package identifiers, and FHIR-42068 resolved the AdministrableProductDefinition PhPID/code issue as AdministrableProductDefinition.classification rather than APD.code; FHIR-42068 is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current source already has the requested MedicinalProductDefinition.code element and explanatory identifier/code definitions, and adding broader code elements or duplicate prose under FHIR-31794 would go beyond the final applied decision.

related_jiras.note: Clarified PackagedProductDefinition identifier distinctions and helped bound the package-resource part of this investigation.
Later APD PhPID/code concern was resolved as AdministrableProductDefinition.classification and was already published on the combined branch.
